title: Salt March to Dandi
summary: On 12 March 1930 Gandhi led 78 satyagrahis from Sabarmati Ashram near Ahmedabad on a 241-mile march to the Gujarat coast. They reached Dandi on 5 April, and on 6 April he picked up salt, defying the British salt law. Millions followed in breaking the law; Gandhi was arrested on 4 May 1930.

uncertainty.note: mkgandhi.org says the march ended on 5 April 1930 and salt was picked up on 6 April. Other pages found in search gave 6 April as the end, but only the two opened pages are cited.

as_recorded.value: The long 241 mile trek finally ended on April 5, 1930
On April 6, the atmosphere at Dandi was both tense and solemn
In 1930, Mahatma Gandhi made the decision to oppose the British Government

where.modern_name: Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad, to Dandi, Navsari district, Gujarat, India (start point shown)
where.historical_name: Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad, to Dandi, a seaside village in Gujarat, under British rule

waypoints.label: Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad: the march begins at 6.30 a.m. with 78 satyagrahis.
Borsad: Gandhi addresses a gathering on 18 March (city centre point).
Dandi: the march ends 5 April; salt law broken 6 April (point is the National Salt Satyagraha Memorial).

importance.justification: Landmark act of nonviolent civil disobedience that spread across India against the salt law.

reviewer_note: Only three waypoints have dates on opened pages (12 March start, 18 March Borsad, 5-6 April Dandi); the route between them is not traced. Distance is 241 miles (mkgandhi.org) vs 390 km (Gujarat Tourism). Marcher count 78 (mkgandhi.org) vs 80 (Gujarat Tourism). Pin for Dandi is the memorial.

beats.caption: Gandhi sets out from Sabarmati Ashram at 6.30 a.m. with 78 marchers, heading for the sea at Dandi.
The column reaches Borsad on 18 March; across the 241 miles it halts for the night at 22 places.
On 6 April Gandhi picks up salt at Dandi, breaking the salt law; millions follow, and salt depots are raided.
